newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil creeps up, barges regain confidence.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil creeps up, barges regain confidence.

text.p: Fuel oil was stronger again on Friday underpinned by tight supplies and a cargo trade nearly $2 up on the last done.

High sulphur barge trade began at $122.50 fob ARA and went as high as $125 with the market assessed at $123-125. There was strong buying, but only average physical bunker demand. Dealers said confidence had returned after the price drops on Thursday.
High sulphur cargoes were a touch higher after a deal done at $117 fob NWE between two traders. Some said the price looked inflated against the $115.50 fob NWE done yesterday.

"It looks engineered, but if its genuine then fair enough," said one trader at a major. Prices were firmer on the back of the deal at $116-117 fob NWE. High sulphur was still thinly offered which with Romanian demand for up to 1.2 million tonnes this winter ensured firm prices.

Low sulphur cargoes were broadly unchanged at $126-128 fob NWE. The main Med buyer was thought in discussion for a further cargo having purchased two 45-50kt cargoes and one 30kt parcel this week. Low sulphur consumption in Italy was seen high in September, indicating possible stock replenishment.
